lesson.title: Variables & Data Types
lesson.subtitle: Learn how to store and manage data in Java.
lesson.theory_text: In Java, a variable is a container for storing data values. To create a variable, you must specify its type and assign a value to it using the equals sign (=). Common types include int for whole numbers and String for text.

lesson.title: Operators & Expressions
lesson.subtitle: Perform arithmetic and logical operations.
lesson.theory_text: Operators are special symbols used to perform operations on variables and values. In Java, arithmetic operators handle math (+, -, *, /, %), relational operators compare values (==, >, <), and logical operators evaluate boolean conditions (&&, ||, !).

lesson.title: Control Flow - If / Else
lesson.subtitle: Control the program flow based on states.
lesson.theory_text: Control flow statements allow you to dictate the order in which code executes based on conditions. Common control flow statements include if-else statements, switch statements, and loops (for, while).

lesson.title: Loops - For & While
lesson.subtitle: Repeat code execution efficiently.
lesson.theory_text: Loops are used to execute a block of code repeatedly as long as a specified condition is true. Common types of loops in Java include for loops, while loops, and do-while loops.

lesson.title: Arrays
lesson.subtitle: Manage ordered lists of elements.
lesson.theory_text: An array is a data structure that can hold multiple values of the same type. In Java, arrays are declared with a specific size and can be accessed using an index, starting from 0.

lesson.title: Methods
lesson.subtitle: Structure your application with functions and scope.
lesson.theory_text: A method is a block of code that performs a specific task and can be called upon when needed. Methods can take parameters, return values, and help organize code into reusable sections.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a method in Java?
options: To perform a specific task and can be reused
questions.explanation: Hint: Methods help structure modular code so you do not have to rewrite the same logic.

lesson.title: Classes & Objects
lesson.subtitle: Build object-oriented structures in Java.
lesson.theory_text: In Java, a class is a blueprint for creating objects. An object is an instance of a class that can have attributes (fields) and behaviors (methods). Classes encapsulate data and functionality, promoting modularity and reusability.

questions.question_text: What is the relationship between a class and an object in Java?
options: A class is an instance of an object
An object is a blueprint for a class
A class is a blueprint for creating objects
questions.explanation: Hint: Think of the class as the architectural blueprint and the object as the built house.
